A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SongBloom and contain complete, readable main text and appendices A–C. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support comparison of the equations, five tables, and three figures.

before.justification: v3 reports original objective and listening-test results in Tables 2–3, conditioning ablations in Table 4, sensitivity experiments in Figures 2–3, and sketch-representation experiments in Appendix A.

after.justification: v4 retains these original evaluations and ablations, including the experimental results in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The interleaved generation procedure, architecture, conditioning, and joint training objective are retained. The added logit-normal time-sampling description documents a training detail without establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both use the same reported 100K-hour Chinese/English song corpus and evaluate lyric-to-song generation using generated lyrics and reference clips from unseen songs. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 retain the same comparators: Suno-v4.5, Udio-v1.5, Haimian, Mureka-O1, ACE-step, YuE-7B, DiffRhythm-full, and SongEditor. Changed footnote markers do not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: Sample selection, model configurations, training budgets, inference settings, metrics, and Appendix C listening criteria are unchanged. The newly disclosed sampling distribution and commercial-comparison date do not establish revised experimental procedures.

E4.justification: Both retain the diffusion-conditioning ablations in Table 4, patch-size and diffusion-step analyses in Figures 2–3, and sketch-choice ablations in Appendix A/Table 5. Their experimental questions and evidence are unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 3 retains identical plus/minus uncertainty summaries. Neither version adds or revises repeated-run counts, seeds, uncertainty-estimation explanations, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 2–5 retain the same result entries and numerical values, and Figures 2–3 are identical. For example, SongBloom-full-ft retains PER 5.49% and FAD 3.20 in Table 2. Reported qualitative findings also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation (9) removes the explicit z^i ~ p(a) qualifier from the expectation, and the accompanying text specifies the diffusion-time distribution pi_t as logit-normal. This is a limited revision of the mathematical loss specification; the remaining equations and Appendix B complexity derivation are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and concluding discussion retain the same contributions and performance claims: unified interleaved generation, coherent full-length songs, superiority to noncommercial baselines, and competitiveness with Suno-v4.5.

C2.justification: Table 2 newly qualifies commercial-platform results as valid until June 23, 2025, adding a specific temporal boundary to those comparisons. The mechanism interpretations, applicability discussion, and Section 7 limitations otherwise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 newly discloses logit-normal diffusion-time sampling with an attribution, but removes Table 2's identification of the Hugging Face Space used to generate ACE-step samples. Hardware, other hyperparameters, and SongBloom code/demo access information are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds Esser et al., Scaling Rectified Flow Transformers for High-Resolution Image Synthesis, to support its time-sampling choice. Other cited works and the substantive related-work positioning are retained; subsequent citation numbers shift.

P1.justification: v4 adds an acknowledgment section, identifies Haizhou Li as another corresponding author, updates the publication footer to NeurIPS 2025, and makes limited grammatical and terminology edits. The main narrative and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 2's caption and footnotes change, and references reflow around the acknowledgment. v4 introduces mismatched markers: Suno carries the dagger whose note describes DiffRhythm, while DiffRhythm carries an unmatched double dagger. Figures and table structures are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: Specifying logit-normal time sampling reduces ambiguity in the core training description, and dating the commercial comparisons clarifies their scope. These provide a modest overall gain, despite the removed ACE-step source disclosure and incorrect Table 2 footnote markers. The experimental evidence and appendix analyses remain unchanged.
